conclusion: pT,10 is an outer equal-height momentum coordinate, and K_tail compares two finite-interval logarithmic slopes of the same integrated coherent spectrum; neither requires an exponential fit.
backend: Python/matplotlib, following the existing shape-scan figure workflow

panels.single: Semilogarithmic peak-normalized yield versus pT squared; three outer peak-height crossings, two secants, and only symbolic pT,f squared and B labels.

style: Match the existing physics manuscript: serif text and STIX math, boxed axes, inward major/minor ticks on four sides, black spectrum, thin grey guides, restrained dashed/dash-dot secants. No title, prose, numerical parameter blocks, arrows, shaded bands, or explanatory legend. Conditions and definitions belong in the caption.
primary_reference: The saved no-skin spherical full spectrum used for the current Fig. 8, b=12-60 fm, |y|<1, finest saved b step 0.5 fm.
separate_diagnostic: The saved free-space-field no-skin spherical calculation, b=12-10000 fm, |y|<1; never substituted for the Fig. 8 reference.
spectrum: dN/d(pT squared), proportional to the azimuth-averaged coherent intensity with no radial pT Jacobian; b/y integrated before peak normalization.
crossing_convention: Saved-node peak and linear interpolation of the yield in pT on the same descending branch before the first upturn.
uncertainty: Deterministic spherical reference. No orientation MC error; numerical quadrature, detector, event-count and model uncertainties are not represented.
review_risks: pT,f labels denote percentages of peak height, not cumulative-yield quantiles.
Monotonic decrease in pT squared does not imply a single exponential in pT squared.
K_tail=1 means equal interval-averaged slopes and does not prove a globally exponential curve.
A decrease of K_tail alone need not imply a decrease of the absolute B_tail.
The baseline R=5.02 fm and a=0.46 fm matches Fig. 8's registered scan and is not the original manuscript Woods-Saxon table.
